prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro: underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hour patterns. Communications-Based Train Control system (CBTC) supervises separation/authority/regulation. Line Traffic Controller authorizes/coordin­ates service/recovery; Revenue Train Operator handles readiness/cab/passengers/instructions; Voice Dispatch Console supports non-vital degraded coordination. Metro Operations Control System (Lantern): positions/regulation/alarms/commands; sends Crew Login Token Bundle. Service Timetable Server supplies non-vital schedules. Passenger Information Gateway receives non-vital position/service state, distributes approved messages; no safety influence. North District Zone Controller (Marble): northern mainline/turnback/East Junction Interlocking approach. South District Zone Controller (Orchid): southern mainline/turnback/West Junction Interlocking approach. Controllers derive safe authority from location/occupancy/field state; boundary uses track ownership/radio overlap/receiving-zone authority reissue. Interlockings control vital points/signals, accept safety-compliant commands; indications reach onboard. Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel): validates authority sequence/applicability/consistency; supervises speed/protection/doors/commands. Activation requires authentication/energization/valid integrity. Modes: initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train/fallback/cutout. Recalculates braking each enforcement cycle; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log after enforcement-data validation. Dual Channel Odometer supplies independent speed/distance; excessive divergence degrades confidence, increases uncertainty/separation-preserving requests. Trainborne propulsion/braking interface converts safety commands with non-vital isolation; brake assurance monitors feedback/pressure/deceleration. Train Radio Modem maintains onboard bearer via Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron): overlapping station/tunnel/crossover/depot coverage, especially throats/interlocking approaches; reports quality/registration/continuity before minimum margin. Prefer make-before-break handover after acceptance/message checks; rapid degradation invokes last validated authority, never unverified data. Safety Data Communication Network transports vital controller/interlocking/interface messages: deterministic routing, integrity/authentication/bounded monitored latency, physical/logical non-vital separation; sends Clock Drift Sample Report at synchronization intervals. Operator interface displays authority/speed/confidence/radio/actions; rejects stale/inconsistent acknowledgements. Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges enable/closed-and-locked indications when berthed. Maintenance Diagnostic Server (Quarry) collects non-vital health for Signal Maintenance Engineer (Maple); no vital/bypass access. Cyber Security Officer oversees access/security.

New part:
S066: At a zone boundary, the Atlas Onboard Controller confirms train position from the Dual Channel Odometer before accepting the next authority source.
S067: The receiving zone validates route state, train identity, and the expected boundary track section before extending authority beyond the transfer point.
S068: East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking report switch state, track occupancy, and route locking status to the responsible zone controller through vital interfaces.
S069: Wayside supervision compares interlocking indications, train position reports, and radio session state to detect inconsistent conditions before they can affect service.
S070: When the comparison detects a mismatch, the affected authority is withheld or shortened until the condition is resolved under the applicable operating rule.
S071: Metro Operations Control System displays zone status, radio coverage alarms, and train supervision states so that Line Traffic Controller can manage service without direct intervention in vital logic.
S072: Maintenance Diagnostic Server receives non-vital summaries of radio and network health, which allows Signal Maintenance Engineer to investigate degraded coverage trends without connecting to the vital channels.
S073: Wayside Radio Access Network sends the Radio Handover Audit File after each configured reporting interval.
S074: Voice Dispatch Console remains available as an operational communication path, but it is not used as a substitute for safety data messages or zone controller validation.
S075: Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges only the permitted interface indications with the supervising wayside systems, and its state is not allowed to override movement authority logic.
S076: Passenger Information Gateway and Service Timetable Server may receive selected service information, but those non-vital outputs are isolated from the command paths used for train protection.
S077: The CBTC supervision boundary at junctions is defined by the commanded route state, detected point position, and confirmed track vacancy rather than by geographic chainage alone.
S078: East Junction Interlocking is also known locally as Falcon for maintenance callouts and legacy panel references.
S079: North District Zone Controller requests routes through East Junction Interlocking only when the requested path is consistent with the current movement authority and the train approach profile.
S080: South District Zone Controller applies the same route protection principles for interfaces with West Junction Interlocking, including checks on flank protection and conflicting movement locking.
S081: The interlocking retains final vital authority for point movement, point locking, route locking, and release of protected sections.
S082: CBTC supervision treats a route as available only after the relevant interlocking reports points detected, locked, and proved in the required position.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
